attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: Witness canonicalization is semantic; it is not available from the selector circuit alone and can be bypassed by list-wise OR evaluation.
steps: Start with an approximate t-list selector A_N and attempt to pick the lexicographically first selected satisfiable query.
To choose that index the circuit must know SAT labels on all selected formulas, so the reduction imports a promise solver S_N on U_A.
Once S_N is imported, the decision circuit ORs the t answers and no longer needs a single witness index.
The cost is C(A_N)+t_N C(S_N)+exception correction, which can be subthreshold even if every single selector is hard.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This proves only a necessary leakage gate and a falsifier condition. It gives no lower bound on Lambda_N^{list} and therefore no separation such as P != NP.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: approximate list-selector leakage gate

assumptions: epsilon>0 is fixed and the claimed source lower bound is C(H_N)>N^{1+epsilon-o(1)} in unrestricted nonuniform circuits.
The batched generator interface can expose all selected formulas with cost N^rho+N^{tau+o(1)}; if only per-query generation is available, replace rho by rho+tau in the leakage bound.
A_N has circuit size N^a, S_N has circuit size N^b as measured after restricting to L_N-bit formulas but parameterized by N, and |E_A|<=N^delta.
The exception correction circuit may use nonuniform equality advice for E_A and costs O(N|E_A|).
definitions: source object: H_N(x)=OR_{j<M_N} SAT(G_N(x,j)) on N-bit inputs, with M_N=N^q, SAT query length L_N=(log N)^d for fixed d>1, and batched generator circuit size at most N^rho.
target object: SAT on L_N-bit formulas; the target consequence of a valid H_N lower bound is SAT notin P/poly when q,rho<1+epsilon and the bridge holds for every fixed SAT circuit exponent.
controlled interface: a target SAT circuit of size L_N^c is substituted only through the generated query list, giving H_N circuits of size N^{max{rho,q}+o(1)} and no uncharged advice.

target-preserving condition: q<1+epsilon, rho<1+epsilon, d>1, and every selector, promise solver, selected generator, and exception table used to simplify H_N is charged in the same nonuniform SIZE model.

An approximate t-list selector A_N outputs at most t_N=N^tau indices. Its miss set E_A contains x with H_N(x)=1 but no selected index j has SAT(G_N(x,j))=1, together with points where the selected-image solver is wrong after composition.

The selected image U_A is {G_N(x,j): x in {0,1}^N and j appears in A_N(x)}. A promise solver S_N is valid on U_A if it agrees with SAT on every formula in U_A, or outside an explicitly charged exceptional preimage set.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The derivation does not rule out high-sensitivity, nonconstructive, non-large, or nonblack-box separators; it only quarantines low-global-sensitivity proof objects. The sharper polylog-sensitivity threshold needs a cited certificate bound exponent h.
steps: Assume R_N is total, poly(N)-constructive, R_N(x*)=1, and R_N rejects TT(SIZE(m^k)).
Apply a sensitivity-to-certificate theorem to obtain a set I of at most B(s_N) coordinates such that every y agreeing with x* on I satisfies R_N(y)=1.
The accepting cylinder {y:y_I=x*_I} has uniform density 2^{-|I|} >= 2^{-B(s_N)}.
If B(s_N)<=a log_2 N, the property has density at least N^{-a}; constructivity is already poly(N), and usefulness is exactly the rejection of TT(SIZE(m^k)).
Therefore the route produces a valid natural property useful against SIZE(m^k), not a P != NP proof.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: It is a barrier audit. It shows that one class of lower-bound certificates would contradict standard PRF-based natural-proof expectations, while leaving the main P != NP conjecture untouched.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Barrier-Aware Lower-Bound Route: global-sensitivity naturalization gate

assumptions: Use a sensitivity-to-certificate theorem giving C_1(R_N,x) <= B(s_N) for every accepted input x.
For an elementary unconditional version, B(s)=s 2^{s-1}, enough when s_N <= log_2 log_2 N - log_2 log_2 log_2 N - O(1).
For a sharper version, insert any established polynomial bound B(s)=s^h from sensitivity/certificate-complexity inequalities; the exact exponent h must be cited before use.
Usefulness is full: every SIZE(m^k) truth table is rejected, not merely most circuits or a sampled subfamily.
definitions: source object: A total Boolean property R_N over N-bit truth tables, decidable in poly(N), with global sensitivity s_N=max_x |{i:R_N(x) != R_N(x^i)}|.
target object: The set TT(SIZE(m^k)) of N-bit truth tables of m-input Boolean functions computed by circuits of size at most m^k, with N=2^m.
controlled interface: R_N(TT(SAT_m))=1 and R_N(y)=0 for every y in TT(SIZE(m^k)); no promise inputs are allowed.
target-preserving condition: The truth-table encoding, constructivity algorithm, and sensitivity bound are uniform in N, and padding/advice cannot change the rejected target class.

equations.label: positive_certificate_bound
equations.valid_when: Valid when R_N is total over all N-bit truth tables and s_N bounds global sensitivity.

equations.label: accepting_subcube_density
equations.valid_when: Valid when the positive certificate fixes coordinates and every extension remains accepted by R_N.

equations.label: natural_largeness_threshold
equations.valid_when: Applies when the certificate-size threshold is logarithmic in the full truth-table length N.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A route survives this lemma only by showing B(s_N)=omega(log N), nonconstructivity, nonuniform leakage in the interface, or a non-natural/nonblack-box feature that invalidates the PRF falsifier.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Barrier bridge lemma: converts low global sensitivity of a SAT separator into polynomial-density naturalness with the same target usefulness.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Let R_N:{0,1}^N->{0,1} be a poly(N)-constructive truth-table property with global sensitivity s_N. If R_N accepts TT(SAT_m), rejects every truth table computed by SIZE(m^k), N=2^m, and the sensitivity-certificate bound B(s_N) is O(log N), then R_N is a valid Razborov-Rudich natural property useful against SIZE(m^k). Thus any SAT lower-bound route whose proof object is such an R_N is blocked by the natural-proof/PRF falsifier unless it is non-large, nonconstructive, non-useful, or outside the PRF regime.

assumptions: Let x*=TT(SAT_m) and Q_N(y)=1 iff y=x*.
Checking Q_N is poly(N) because each SAT bit on m-bit formulas can be recomputed in time 2^{O(m)}=poly(N).
definitions: source object: A property Q_N over N-bit truth tables with small total influence under the uniform measure.
target object: Any proposed natural-proof carrier that tries to infer density from average sensitivity rather than certificates.
controlled interface: Q_N may contain a distinguished explicit truth table but need not contain an accepting subcube.
target-preserving condition: Constructivity must be measured in poly(N), so equality to an explicit exponential-time truth table is allowed as a property test.

candidate_lemmas.statement: Low average sensitivity or low total influence alone does not imply natural largeness for truth-table properties.

target object: TT(SIZE(m^k)) under the same N=2^m encoding.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No construction is known for a uniform, cap-compatible, low-entropy MCSP source with constant epsilon and a proved existential hard accepted certificate on kappa-dense lengths.
steps: Define A_m by the uniform verifier V and choose ell_m with |A_m|<=2^{ell_m}<=2^{h m+O(1)}.

Construct F_m on inputs (a,z): enumerate certificates in lexicographic order, find the a-th accepted certificate if it exists, sequentially compute the z-th emitted bit, and output zero for missing rows.
The decision procedure runs in 2^{O(m)} time; since n_m=m+ell_m=O(m), the target family is in E when ell_m and the length schedule are uniform.
If a circuit C of size S computes F_m, fix a to the hard accepted certificate y*. The restricted circuit computes T_{y*}, so S>2^{epsilon m}-O(n_m).
Convert the bound to the target input length: for every eta>0, CC(F_m)>2^{(epsilon/(1+h)-eta)n_m} for large m.
Use kappa-dense padding to cover all target lengths, yielding any delta<epsilon/((1+h)kappa).
Audit the source against the verifier cap alpha_V; a claim epsilon>alpha_V is invalid before extraction.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The derivation is a valid conditional bridge inside E lower-bound machinery, not a construction of the required MCSP source and not a proof of P != NP.

assumptions: epsilon>0 and h>=0 are constants or uniformly computable limsup bounds.
For infinitely many or kappa-dense m, A_m contains a certificate y whose emitted m-bit truth table has circuit complexity greater than 2^{epsilon m}.
Membership in A_m and sequential bit emission of T_y are decidable in 2^{O(m)} time, with no nonuniform selector or per-length advice.
The verifier checkpoint profile has cap alpha_V, so a claimed source threshold above alpha_V is invalid.
definitions: source object: A uniform MCSP-certificate verifier V which, on length m, has an accepted set A_m of O(m)-bit certificates; at least one y in A_m emits a truth table T_y with circuit complexity greater than 2^{epsilon m}.
target object: An E-uniform multiplexed language F on n_m=m+ell_m input bits, later padded to all target lengths, with circuit lower bound 2^{delta n}.
controlled interface: Lexicographic accepted-certificate unranking maps row index a to y_a, and F_m(a,z)=T_{y_a}(z) while rows beyond |A_m| are filled with zero.
target-preserving condition: V, the entropy bound ell_m<=h m+O(1), the source length schedule, and padding map are uniform, and the reduction preserves density, threshold, and absence of advice.
